To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) there are no legal provisions in Turkey that regulate domestic work, (ii) the lack of legal provisions in the field of domestic work has led to the exclusion of domestic workers from social policy, (iii) the social policy measures that do not include domestic workers are not only discriminatory but also contribute to their social exclusion and (iv) the social policy that excludes domestic workers also leads to the exclusion of their employers from social policy.
domestic work is not a profession, but a job.
domestic workers in Turkey are a vulnerable group, that they are not included in the scope of social protection and that they are not protected by labour law.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the following questions. What is the legal framework that regulates the employment relationship between employers and domestic workers? What kind of social protection is available to domestic workers
how the social policy framework and the social policy process affect the lives of domestic workers and how they are perceived and treated in the social policy process.
the social policy implications of the legal status of domestic work and domestic workers in Turkey.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there are still many problems in Turkey in terms of the legal status of domestic work and domestic workers.
the current legal framework in Turkey is inadequate to protect domestic workers.
the current social policy framework in the country is not sufficient in terms of protecting domestic workers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
domestic work is a gendered and class-based form of work.
there is no specific social policy for the domestic workers in Turkey.

domestic workers are not covered by the social protection system in Turkey and they have no social rights and benefits as workers, and that the social policy approach is not sufficient for the recognition of the domestic workers as workers.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the current situation is characterized by a lack of legal protection, a lack of social policy measures and a lack of recognition of domestic work as work.
domestic workers are a group of workers that is not covered by any social security legislation.
